text:
maia: Heads up — since ~08:10 UTC we're seeing a spike of 429s for /v1/rerank in eu-west. Error rate up to 4.2% and p95 latency creeping 2x. Not seeing obvious infra OOMs.

josh: noticed that too. Embedding lanes are at 92% util on the dedicated pool. Rerank is on the same physical GPU pool with hashed routing; maybe congestion on the rerank path.

ops-bot: [alert] 429 spike detected for service=redwood-rerank region=eu-west window=5m rate=4.2% p95_latency=230ms

maia: That's the thing — the host-level GPU mem is fine, but queue depth for rerank worker pods is piling up. I think the admission control knob 'token_weight' for rerank was lowered last week and we may be letting more small-requests through that hurt batching.

leah: Can you paste the grafana panel link? curious which tenants are spiking.

maia: grafana: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/9H2k3L/rerank-lanes?orgId=1&from=now-15m

vikram: From logs — ~60% of 429s are coming from two high-traffic customers hitting short-seq rerank jobs (~1-2k requests/min). They normally go to the "fast" lane but are being hashed to the same shard as heavy embedding fanout.

josh: Proposed quick fixes: 1) soft-quota those tenants on rerank path (per-tenant inflight cap) 2) enable spillover routing to backup rerank lane (non-dedicated but lower cost) 3) bump rerank admission token weight back to previous value. Which one do we want first?

maia: Let's do minimal blast radius: (2) enable spillover routing to backup lane for those two tenants + (3) revert token_weight to last week's value. Apply (1) if spillover doesn't reduce 429s.

oncall-sre: I'm happy to patch the admission config and trigger routing toggle. Will need a short maintenance window (1 min) to flip the routing rule.

josh: Config snippet to flip (will apply to eu-west service-config namespace):

```yaml
admission_control:
  rerank:
    token_weight: 1.5        # revert from 1.1 -> 1.5
    per_tenant_inflight: 120 # keep greater than default, used only if soft-quota enabled
routing:
  rerank:
    spillover_enabled: true
    spillover_policy: "tenant-whitelist" # only for high-traffic tenants
    spillover_targets: ["backup-rerank-eu"]
```

leah: +1. Also let's add a short-term metric to track 'spillover_rate' and 'rerank_429_by_tenant' so we know if the hotspot migrates.

ops-bot: [deploy] PR #4219 merged by josh — admission_control change staged to canary.

maia: Canary looks ok for 5m. p50/p95 improved for canary shards. Rolling to eu-west now.

oncall-sre: Rolling routing toggle in 30s. I'll monitor the cluster egress and the dedicated pool util.

vikram: After toggle, we're seeing immediate drop in 429s from 4.2% -> 0.6%. rerank queue depth reduced by ~70% on hot shards.

josh: Nice. Still seeing some tail 429s for a couple tenants — enabling per-tenant soft-quota for them now to limit new inflight to 80.

maia: Can we add a short-term rule to prefer KV-cache hits for rerank when available? Hot tenants have good cache rates; that will reduce compute. 

leah: Filed a follow-up: https://tasks.redwood/ENG-1728 — add prefect cache preference + spillover autoscaling policy.

oncall-sre: Postmortem action items draft: 1) revert token_weight change review process, 2) implement automatic tenant-driven spillover thresholds, 3) dashboard for rerank 429 by hashed-shard. I'll post draft in #postmortems.

maia: TL;DR — cause: hashed routing + lowered token_weight created contention between embedding fanout and rerank on same shard. Fix: spillover routing + revert token_weight + tenant soft-quota. Monitoring shows healthy after fixes. :thumbsup:

josh: +1, closing thread. If we see recurrence we'll consider separating physical pools for rerank and heavy-embed customers (costy, but doable).
